item.title: ICLC 2027: International Conference on Live Coding, Call for Participation (Dialogues)
item.description:
Organisation: Lambdasonic (TOPLAP Belgium), Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel

Location: Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel International Arts Center, Antwerp, Belgium. Open to anyone engaged with live coding; remote participation considered.

Award: NO submission fee. The call does not state artist fees, travel support or accommodation for accepted contributors, so budget for self-funded attendance unless the organisers announce otherwise. Proceedings are published with a DOI per article. Satellite-event hosts can request a Letter of Intent to support their own local funding applications.

Duration: Five-day conference, 9 to 13 March 2027. Workshops are 2 hours (short) or 4 hours (long).

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The International Conference on Live Coding is dedicated to practices and research focused on technologies and philosophies that interpret the use of computer code and the public writing of algorithms as performative gestures. The 10th edition runs 9 to 13 March 2027 in Antwerp, hosted by Lambdasonic (TOPLAP Belgium) with the Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel. THEME: 'Dialogues', framing live coding as continuous improvisational exchange between coder, machine and audience, and across disciplines. Suggested topics include dialogues between live coding and acoustic musicians, dancers, theatre, classically trained musicians reading live-coded (or graphical) scores, band and jazz-combo settings, live-coder ensembles, ten-minute live-coded mini-operas, DMX lighting systems, graphics and shader live coding, robotics (pen plotters, textile-weaving robots), design-as-performance, community building, diversity/equity/inclusion, accessibility of live coding languages and interfaces, education, and algorave. The venues will facilitate collaborations with resident dancers, a jazz combo (back-line provided: drums, guitar amp, bass amp, piano), a string quartet reading scores a prima vista, visual artists, students and researchers where possible. FORMATS: short papers (2-4 pages) and long papers (5-12 pages) using the provided template; live performances (800-word abstract, max 150-word programme note, technical rider); workshops (short 2h or long 4h, max 700-word abstract, held in English or Dutch); installations (max 700-word abstract, technical questionnaire plus a measured plan or sketch, with the interactive aspect clearly defined); and satellite events. All contributors submit a max 150-word biography. Peer review is single-blind with at least two reviewers per submission. LANGUAGE: submissions must be in English, except that live performance, installation and workshop proposals may also be submitted in another language (workshops: English, Dutch or French) with a machine-translated English version, stated as such. Substantial use of generative AI in writing papers and performance abstracts must be disclosed; proofreading and translation are exempt. In-person presentation is encouraged, with remote proposals considered and sessions live-streamed where possible; the organisers ask attendees to minimise travel impact and to link up with nearby satellite events to turn a long trip into a mini-tour. The call notes attention to access needs, care responsibilities and other barriers to participation. SATELLITE EVENTS: live coding nodes, art schools and other organisations worldwide are invited to host their own events before or after ICLC 2027; submit a declaration of interest via Fourwaves before 1 February 2027 with a principal contact, city and any confirmed details, and join #iclc-satellite-events on the TOPLAP Discord. Hosts are asked to seek local funding for accommodation, travel and artist fees; the committee cannot fund or organise these but will coordinate dates and publish your event. TO APPLY: submit via Fourwaves at https://event.fourwaves.com/iclc2027/pages using the templates at https://codeberg.org/iclc/iclc-templates (read the README for full proposal instructions). Submission deadline extended to 1 September 2026; acceptance notification 1 November 2026. CALL FOR REVIEWERS: anyone active in a live-coding-related field can volunteer by emailing a short description and keywords of their expertise to iclc@lambdasonic.be, the same address for general questions.

item.title: ESWA Digital Rights Gathering 2026: The (W)horrors Edition (Barcelona)
item.description:
Organisation: European Sex Workers' Rights Alliance (ESWA)

Location: Barcelona, Spain. Gathering runs 2-5 November 2026 (travel day out 1 November, travel day home 5 November).

Award: PARTICIPANTS: fully funded, with travel, accommodation and food covered for all selected participants. SESSION FACILITATORS: EUR 300 per 90-minute session, plus travel, accommodation and meals covered. Free to apply.

Duration: Three days of sessions, 2-4 November 2026, within a 1-5 November travel window

Deadline: Rolling / undated

NO PUBLISHED CLOSING DATE: the call gives no application deadline, so the operative cutoff is the gathering itself on 2-5 November 2026; apply early. The European Sex Workers' Rights Alliance (ESWA) brings back its Digital Rights Gathering in 2026 as The (W)horrors Edition, in Barcelona just after Halloween. It is a capacity and community-building space by and for sex workers, convened to confront the surveillance, censorship and digital violence they face online and to imagine and build more resilient digital futures. A limited number of spaces is reserved for allies working in adjacent digital rights and harm reduction spaces to host sessions. TWO CALLS ARE OPEN. (1) CALL FOR PARTICIPANTS, for sex workers who want to deepen their knowledge of digital rights, online safety and community resilience. Requirements: be a current or former sex worker who is also a member of an organisation in ESWA's network; be available for three days of interactive sessions, skill-sharing and collective learning on 2, 3 and 4 November, and free from 1 November (travel out) through 5 November (travel home), even though some final-day sessions are optional. Selected participants receive full funding covering travel, accommodation and food. (2) CALL FOR TRAINERS AND SESSION PROPOSALS, for facilitators, trainers and educators experienced in digital rights, online safety or sex worker-led organising, who want to deliver an interactive workshop, skill-share or creative session. Sessions run 90 minutes and are compensated at EUR 300 per session, with travel, accommodation and meals covered. Open to current or former sex workers, and to allies with experience in digital rights, digital discrimination, digital security and related fields. SESSION STRANDS: Digital (W)horrors, naming the threats faced online and unpacking how surveillance, censorship and platform policy work against sex workers, including shadowbanning and algorithmic censorship, over-zealous content moderation, law enforcement and third-party surveillance, deplatforming, non-consensual data scraping and retention, and the platforms and policies that enable them; Building Resilience, practical hands-on skills covering open source and privacy-respecting software, how and why to divest from Big Tech platforms, alternative and encrypted communication tools, digital security basics such as protecting data, devices and identity, and other harm-reduction strategies for working and organising online; Imagining Better Futures, creative forward-looking sessions on what a sex worker friendly internet would look like, including prototyping inclusive digital tools, platforms and spaces built by and for sex workers, new apps, alternative social platforms, community-owned tech, and speculative design exercises; Resourcing the Group, sessions focused on care and resilience, including writing and reflection, grounding and somatic exercises, tools for self-care and sustainability in activism, and space for radical rest. The organisers welcome grounded, political and creative contributions from anyone who would like to lead a session. Separate application forms for participants and for session proposals are linked from the call page. Questions: ana@eswalliance.org.

item.title: INHABIT #16 and #17: Artist-in-Residence 2027 (Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics)
item.description:
Organisation: Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics

Location: Frankfurt am Main, Germany

Award: Artist's fee of EUR 8,000 plus an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a production budget depending on the project, and travel costs to and within Frankfurt. Also included: realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the institute's library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support throughout the residency. No application fee.

Duration: Four months. Two slots: INHABIT #16 runs April to July 2027, INHABIT #17 runs September to December 2027

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

INHABIT is the artist-in-residence programme of the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics in Frankfurt am Main, which invites artists from various disciplines to collaborate with its scientists and researchers, treating artistic thinking and knowledge as reflective practices in their own right. The 2027 call is addressed to artists from the performing arts and music, who spend four months creating new work, or developing an existing project, inside a scientific research environment and in dialogue with the institute's researchers. Two slots are open for 2027: INHABIT #16 from April to July 2027 and INHABIT #17 from September to December 2027. Work developed during the residency is presented in cooperation with local arts institutions as an exhibition, performance, concert or other format, complemented by discursive formats. WHO THEY ARE LOOKING FOR: artists from the performing arts and music interested in interdisciplinary collaboration between artistic and scientific fields; artists open to developing and sharing a project as an exhibition, performance, concert or another format; and artists active in contemporary culture who respond to the institute with innovative and challenging ideas. WHAT IS OFFERED: an artist's fee of EUR 8,000, an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a project-dependent production budget, travel costs to and in Frankfurt, realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support during the residency. APPLY through the institute's e-recruiting portal by 1 September 2026, 23:59 CET; the jury decision follows in November 2026. No fee.

item.title: Tartu UNESCO City of Literature Residency for Writers and Translators, Autumn 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Estonian Literary Society (Eesti Kirjanduse Selts), Focal Point for Tartu UNESCO City of Literature

Location: Tartu, Estonia. Open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature worldwide.

Award: Monthly stipend of EUR 600 for the two-month stay (EUR 1,200 in total), plus reimbursement of travel costs up to EUR 350. Free accommodation is provided in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment, which has a bedroom, living room, kitchen, bathroom and exhibition room. One resident is selected. No application fee.

Duration: Two months, 15 October to 15 December 2026, with some flexibility on exact dates

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The Estonian Literary Society, which coordinates Tartu UNESCO City of Literature, runs an international residency programme for writers and translators that has hosted authors from Slovenia, Ireland, Hungary, the USA, the UK, Ukraine and Canada since 2017. This is the open call for the autumn 2026 slot: one resident stays two months in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment in Tartu, working on their own writing or translation while connecting with the local literary scene. WHAT THE RESIDENCY OFFERS: a EUR 600 monthly stipend, travel reimbursement up to EUR 350, free accommodation, a local support coordinator to help arrange cultural engagements, and opportunities to perform and present at literary events. The autumn period covers the interdisciplinary literary festival Crazy Tartu on 12 to 14 November, and the resident is offered a slot to perform there alongside writers, poets, musicians and artists from Estonia and abroad. ELIGIBILITY: open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature of any nationality; applicants need an upper-intermediate level of spoken English, at least one published book, screenplay, theatre script or translation from Estonian into another language, a demonstrable interest in Estonian culture and literature, a willingness to take part in local literary activities, and a commitment to working on their own literary project during the stay. HOW TO APPLY: complete the online application form linked from the residency page and upload a fragment of up to five pages of a published text (in Estonian or English) or of a published translation. SELECTION: made by a committee representing the Estonian Literary Society, the Estonian Writers Union, the Estonian Literary Museum and the Tartu Literature House Foundation. Results are announced before 15 September 2026. The programme's stated aims are to enhance international exchange, diversify the local literary scene, introduce new foreign authors and their work to Estonian readers, and build lasting connections beyond the residency period. Questions: Marja Unt, eks@kirjandus.ee. Deadline 1 September 2026.

item.title: Le Garage Moderne: OASIS International Artist Residencies 2026 (Bordeaux)
item.description:
Organisation: Le Garage Moderne (European OASIS project)

Location: Bacalan district, Bordeaux, France. Le Garage Moderne is a non-profit car garage and bicycle workshop, a canteen serving sponsored meals, and a cultural venue housing 11 permanent artists, makers and craftswomen, recently returned to its 19th-century building after a two-and-a-half-year renovation.

Award: Five grants. Each artist receives a fee of EUR 1,300 gross (taxes may apply depending on legal status), up to EUR 600 for production expenses such as raw materials, technical services or special tools, a lump-sum travel grant scaled to distance with top-ups for green travel options, a per diem of EUR 45 per day, and accommodation in a self-catering hotel. Access to the shared tools and spaces of Le Garage Moderne is included, subject to the association's regulations. No application fee.

Duration: Two weeks on site. Five overlapping two-week slots, and applicants may choose one or more: 9 to 22 November, 16 to 29 November, 23 November to 6 December, 30 November to 13 December, and 7 to 20 December 2026. Deadline 1 September 2026; pre-selection interviews 15 September; final selection announced 1 October 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Second year of Le Garage Moderne's residency cycle within the European OASIS project, offering five grants to international artists for two-week stays in Bordeaux. THE SITE IS THE POINT. Le Garage Moderne is a working non-profit car and bicycle workshop with a neighbourhood canteen and a versatile venue for performing arts, concerts and community gatherings, all at once a productive space, a public space and a community-driven common. Having just moved back into its 19th-century building after a long renovation, the team describes machines and workbenches back in place and a brand-new playground, and invites residents to take over the space and explore its physical and social possibilities. They ask for SITE-SPECIFIC PROPOSALS that play with the verticality, the scale of the space, the community and what they call the hive-like vibe of the venue, where everyone runs around, shouts, gets their hands dirty and learns in the process. DISCIPLINES: any, explicitly including design, visual art, performing arts, film, small-scale architecture, emergency architecture, craft-making, street furniture, sound, and interdisciplinary or community-based practices. Proposals combining artistic creation with the spatial and the social are especially encouraged, and the organisers say plainly that they want to be surprised. WHAT IS EXPECTED: openness to exchange and collaboration with the 11 permanent residents and with 3 local artists recruited through a separate OASIS call; participation in 2 days of masterclass open to members and community, where you describe and share your practice, technique and working context with fellow OASIS residents, local artists, members and staff; and a public outcome, which need not be a large event but must be something the public can experience. RIGHTS: work produced during the residency remains the artist's property, but documentation of it is made by Le Garage Moderne and will be publicised by them for three years after the residency. Note this is a different OASIS partner call from the OASis In the Park (Naples) and Disappearing Landscape (High Tatras) rounds under the same European project.

item.title: ITER 2026: International Touring and Environmental Responsibility Programme
item.description:
Organisation: Julie's Bicycle and in futurum, funded by Arts Council England, Arts Council Norway, Creative Scotland and the Danish Arts Foundation

Location: England, Scotland, Norway and Denmark. Seminars run online.

Award: The seminar programme is free to join. Groups of three or more participants can then apply for up to GBP 30,000 for collaborative projects, with funding applications open 6 November 2026 to 11 January 2027 and projects starting spring 2027. No application fee.

Duration: Seminars run weekly from 1 October to 10 December 2026, Tuesdays for Pathfinders and Thursdays for Changemakers, 10:00 to 12:00 UK time. Deadline to join 1 September 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

ITER is now in its fifth year and supports people in the performing arts to build environmentally responsible, inclusive and equitable ways of touring and collaborating internationally. It is initiated and financed by Arts Council England, Arts Council Norway, Creative Scotland and the Danish Arts Foundation, and designed and delivered by Julie's Bicycle and in futurum. Creative Scotland joined as a partner for 2026. TWO TRACKS, up to 60 places in total: PATHFINDERS, ten sessions introducing the principles of sustainable touring for people new to the subject; and CHANGEMAKERS, nine sessions for those further along, on leadership and systemic change. Seminars run weekly from 1 October to 10 December 2026, Pathfinders on Tuesdays and Changemakers on Thursdays, 10:00 to 12:00 UK time, alongside networking and a new alumni network. THE MONEY COMES IN PHASE TWO: after the seminars, groups of three or more participants can apply for up to GBP 30,000 to implement collaborative projects that cut environmental impacts and advance climate justice. Funding applications open 6 November 2026 and close 11 January 2027; awarded projects begin in spring 2027. ELIGIBILITY: based in England, Scotland, Norway or Denmark, working in dance, music or theatre. That covers music and theatre venues receiving touring work, festivals, orchestras, theatre companies, solo artists, performers and musicians, performing arts producers, and multidisciplinary arts organisations. Applications are made through the relevant national funder (Arts Council England open funds, Creative Scotland targeted funding, Arts Council Norway, Danish Arts Foundation). Questions go to environmentaltouring@artscouncil.org.uk.

item.title: IKSV Young Artist Fund: International Circulation Support Programme (Turkey)
item.description:
Organisation: Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts (IKSV)

Location: Turkey; applicants must be Turkish citizens resident in Turkey, departing from and returning to Turkey.

Award: Up to EUR 1,300 per recipient towards documented travel costs (economy flights, trains, buses and public transport; accommodation in some cases). No application fee.

Duration: Travel must take place within one year of the application month

Deadline: Rolling / undated

A standing travel fund from the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts (IKSV) that helps artists, collectives and writers based in Turkey get to international engagements abroad: exhibitions, theatre and dance performances, film screenings, concerts and similar activities. AMOUNT: up to EUR 1,300 towards documented transport costs. Flight support is the priority; economy tickets and public transport only, with accommodation covered in some cases depending on the applicant's budget plan. The fund does not support commercial gallery activity, profit-oriented business models, or personal and tourist travel. WHO CAN APPLY (all must be true): aged 18 to 40; a citizen of the Republic of Turkey; resident in Turkey; departing from and returning to Turkey for the planned trip; applying as an artist, group, collective or initiative; actively producing as a musician, artist, director, performer or writer in music, cinema, performing arts, contemporary art or literature; holding an invitation letter or other document proving the international collaboration; able to justify why the trip matters for professional development; with prior experience of comparable international or national events; and not having received support from this programme in the past year or applied for the same trip already. The hosting institution is expected to be an internationally recognised cultural organisation, and the applicant must be an invited guest, co-organiser or project partner. DEADLINE: applications are open all year and reviewed by an IKSV evaluation panel four times a year, meeting in the last weeks of January, April, July and October, with results announced within 15 days of each meeting. Applications submitted after 14 July 2026 go to the final 2026 panel, planned for late October 2026. HOW TO APPLY: online form at https://forms.gle/NCjyQ7HbncLkawi3A with CV, portfolio (max 10 MB, including performance video for performing arts and music), statement of purpose (max 1,000 characters), one-page budget plan and the invitation letter. All documents as PDF; the invitation letter in English, everything else in Turkish. The open-call page and the application are in Turkish only; there is no English version. Questions: gencsanatcifonu@iksv.org.

item.title: Archipel Butor Livre de dialogue Creation Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Archipel Butor

Location: Lucinges (74380), Haute-Savoie, France, in the house of the writer Michel Butor.

Award: Creation grant of EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, so roughly EUR 4,000 each across the two months and EUR 8,000 for the pair. Up to two return journeys per person are covered within France and Europe. Accommodation is provided in Michel Butor's writer's house. No application fee.

Duration: Two months in total, taken as eight weeks that may be split, starting from January 2027. Time is split 70 percent creation and 30 percent mediation activities.

Deadline: Closed 30 Aug 2026

Archipel Butor runs its creation residency out of the former home of the writer Michel Butor in Lucinges, Haute-Savoie, and this call is for a livre de dialogue, a dialogue book made jointly by a writer and a visual artist. The residency exists to give a pair concentrated time to develop a book together and to raise the profile of artist book culture and of collaboration at the centre of artistic process. WHO APPLIES: a pair made up of an author with a project for a dialogue book and a visual artist collaborating on it. The two do not need to have worked together before, but both must be present during the shared periods. WHAT IS PROVIDED: EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, up to two return trips per person within France and Europe, and accommodation in the writer's house. STRUCTURE: two months in total, taken as eight weeks which may be split across the year from January 2027, with 70 percent of the time given to creation and 30 percent to mediation and public engagement activities. A videoconference is held with the selected laureates beforehand to arrange on-site scheduling and the mediation sessions. HOW TO APPLY: follow the official call document downloadable from the residency page, submitting a single PDF to accueil@archipel-butor.fr containing a joint letter, biographies of both practitioners, the artistic proposal, technical specifications and the proposed mediation activities. NOTE: the call and application file are in French. Deadline 30 August 2026.

item.title: DRIFT: Choreographer Open Call 2026-27 (Dance and Research In The Future Time)
item.description:
Organisation: DRIFT, a four-year Creative Europe cooperation of ten organisations led by Theatre de Liege and Maison de la danse

Location: Activities across Europe: kick-off in Berlin, Festival Lab in Tunis, showcase in Lyon, online labs, plus a residency hosted by your own national DRIFT partner. Applicants must be based in Belgium, France, Germany (Berlin region only), Greece, Norway, Italy, Spain, Ukraine, Tunisia or Portugal, and apply through the partner organisation for their country of residence.

Award: EUR 20,000 research budget per choreographer, covering artistic fees, travel, accommodation and optional collaborator costs. Also included: an Onboarding Lab, two weeks of residency with your national DRIFT partner, three collaborative Online Labs, a Festival Lab in Tunis, individual artistic mentoring and individual curatorial mentoring, and a work-in-progress presentation at the Biennale de la danse in Lyon. No application fee.

Duration: November 2026 to September 2027. Kick-off in Berlin 30 November to 1 December 2026; Festival Lab in Tunis 18-21 March 2027; Biennale de la danse showcase in Lyon 18-25 September 2027.

Deadline: Closed 31 Aug 2026

DRIFT (Dance and Research In The Future Time) is a four-year Creative Europe cooperation between ten European organisations, led by Theatre de Liege and Maison de la danse. The distinguishing feature is that it funds artistic research rather than production: you are expected to arrive with questions, not a finished piece you already intend to make, and reviewers read every section of the application through that lens. STRUCTURE: each of the ten partner organisations selects one choreographer from its own country, forming a cohort of ten. Over the programme you get an Onboarding Lab, two weeks of residency with your national partner, three collaborative Online Labs, a Festival Lab in Tunis, individual artistic and curatorial mentoring, and a work-in-progress showcase at the Biennale de la danse in Lyon, all backed by a EUR 20,000 research budget that covers your fees, travel, accommodation and any collaborators. SECOND PHASE: after a further evaluation, five of the ten artists may receive co-production support and touring across the DRIFT network. That phase is separate from this application and is not guaranteed. ELIGIBILITY: professional choreographers in contemporary dance or performance, at a mid-career stage, meaning an established national practice but not yet fully established internationally. You must be based in Belgium, France, Germany (Berlin region only), Greece, Norway, Italy, Spain, Ukraine, Tunisia or Portugal, and you apply through the partner organisation representing your country of residence, not centrally. Good English and availability for all programme dates are required. The country list is strict, so check it before you start. TIMELINE: applications opened 1 July 2026 and close 31 August 2026; selection through September; results 9 October 2026; programme runs November 2026 to September 2027.

item.title: Scuola Piccola Zattere: International Fellowship and Residency 2027 (Venice)
item.description:
Organisation: Scuola Piccola Zattere

Location: Venice, Italy. Open to any nationality.

Award: EUR 5,000 fellowship grant plus a EUR 2,000 research budget, accommodation in Venice, an individual study space within a shared studio, and round-trip travel to Venice. Collectives and duos share a single grant and one accommodation. No application fee.

Duration: Three months, in one of two slots: early January to early April 2027, or mid-April to mid-July 2027. Applicants may name one slot or indicate availability for both.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Scuola Piccola Zattere is an independent non-profit centre for continuous education and research in the expanded field of contemporary arts, running exhibitions, commissions, fellowships, workshops, seminars, performances and public discussions as one connected research ecosystem rather than separate strands. Two international fellowships are offered. The support is unusually solid for a research fellowship: EUR 5,000 as a grant, EUR 2,000 as a research budget, accommodation, travel and a study space for three months. SEASON THEME: the 2026-2027 cycle is titled Living Document, investigating archives, regulatory documents, collective rituals, games, performative instructions, and the relationship between bodies, architecture and social organisation. Fellows join that shared inquiry while continuing their own work, and are expected to keep an active presence in the institution and contribute to public events through workshops, seminars, presentations, screenings or performances. The fellowship overlaps with the run-up to and opening of the 2027 Architecture Biennale, which is a real advantage if your research benefits from that traffic. ELIGIBILITY: artists, curators, researchers, architects, choreographers, performers and writers of any nationality, as individuals, collectives or duos. Good English is required, and non-EU applicants need a valid passport for international travel. No age limit, but the organisers say it is especially intended for practitioners in the post-academic stage of their career, typically under 40. You must be prepared to spend the full period in Venice, so this is not a remote or partial-attendance fellowship. WHAT THEY WANT: an active research process that can develop through discussion and experimentation, tied to the Living Document theme, not a finished stand-alone project proposal. The motivation letter, portfolio and public programming proposal are read as one integrated application. Deadline 4 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST.

item.title: Connect and Create: Circulation of Performing Arts and Music (Africa-Europe) - 2nd Call
item.description:
Organisation: Goethe-Institut and Expertise France, in collaboration with Institut francais (Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture consortium)

Location: Applicants based in one of the 47 eligible sub-Saharan African countries (Kenya included) or one of the 27 EU Member States. Touring in Africa and/or Europe.

Award: EUR 15,000 to EUR 39,500 per project, covering travel, visas, insurance, accommodation, per diems, local transport and shipping of scenographic and technical elements. No application fee.

Duration: Projects carried out between February and December 2027

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The Circulation strand of Connect and Create funds the touring and dissemination of African artistic creations across Africa and Europe. It is part of the Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture programme (EUR 8M, led by the Goethe-Institut and Expertise France in partnership with Institut francais, supported by the European Union), and is a different strand from the Professional Mobilities call also on the desk. THIS CARD IS THE SECOND CALL, deadline 30 September 2026 (the first call closed 30 November 2025). AMOUNT: EUR 15,000 to EUR 39,500 per project. WHAT IS FUNDED: mobility costs for artistic teams, including transport, visas, insurance, lodging, per diems, local transport, and shipping of scenographic and technical elements. WHO CAN APPLY: artistic teams (performing arts companies, music ensembles, collectives) based in sub-Saharan Africa; dissemination structures (production houses, artist managers, theatres, labels, venues) based in Africa or Europe; and event organisers (festivals, markets, professional gatherings) in Africa or Europe. Applicants must be legally established in one of the 47 eligible sub-Saharan African countries, Kenya among them, or one of the 27 EU Member States. INDIVIDUALS CANNOT APPLY. ELIGIBLE PROJECTS, two formats: (1) TOURS, requiring a minimum of 5 pre-booked dates across at least 3 different African countries, or at least 3 pre-booked dates in one or more European countries; (2) PROGRAMMING WITHIN MAJOR EVENTS, requiring a festival, market or professional gathering in Africa or Europe to host at least 3 artistic teams from different African countries. TIMELINE: activities must take place between February and December 2027; selection committee December 2026, results announced January 2027. PRIORITY is given to projects that build on existing tandems already collaborating, feature emerging artists, use eco-responsible practices, and address inclusion. APPLY via the Institut francais emundus portal. Questions: connectandcreate@expertisefrance.fr.

item.title: transmediale x DARC: Interstices, Research (in) the Gaps, PhD/Research Workshop
item.description:
Organisation: Digital Aesthetics Research Center (DARC), Aarhus University, in collaboration with transmediale

Location: Berlin, Germany; the workshop runs alongside transmediale 2027 (festival 26 to 31 January 2027). Open to researchers based anywhere, inside or outside the academy.

Award: No submission fee. The published call does not state a participation fee, honorarium, travel or accommodation support, so confirm with the organisers before budgeting. Accepted participants present a paper at the workshop and their condensed text is distributed as a newspaper-style article at the festival.

Duration: Research workshop held around transmediale 2027 in Berlin (festival 26 to 31 January 2027)

Deadline: Closed 28 Aug 2026

The annual DARC PhD/Research Workshop, organised by the Digital Aesthetics Research Center at Aarhus University with transmediale, responds to transmediale's 2027 thematic framework. THEME: 'Interstices: Research (in) the gaps'. An interstice is the small space between objects set closely together, the cords in a rope or the atoms in a crystal lattice: an emptiness produced by the structure it belongs to, and without which that structure could not be what it is. In crystallography, interstitial sites are the spaces a lattice and its basis generate but do not fill, and interstitial diffusion, the movement of small atoms through the gaps of a host lattice, is the mechanism by which materials transform. The call asks what the equivalent sites are in social, cultural and computational structures: where are the gaps these combinations generate but do not fill, what moves through them, and do they carry transformative power? It works through Yancey Strickler's dark forest theory of the internet (the withdrawal of meaningful exchange from the open, surveilled, indexed web into private channels), the Dark Forest Collective's anthology and its 'cozyweb' of small sheltered spaces, dark nets, miniverses and moving castles as interstitial spaces produced by and defined against the dominant web, and Bogna Konior's extension of the dark forest metaphor to the opacity of AI systems, where silence is refusal rather than absence and the forest is increasingly inhabited by other-than-human intelligences that opt out of engagement with people. Where big tech pursues efficiency through the automation of human perception, cognition, identification and aesthetics, artists and researchers explore the non/more-than-human, glitchy, noisy, machinic, datafied and dark to build new expression and critique of data-ism and what is marketed as artificial intelligence, including the dangers and potentials inside badly curated data models, between polluting data centres, and in skeuomorphic interfaces. WHAT THEY WANT: proposals from artists, researchers and practitioners for work that occupies and moves through gaps that are social as well as structural, ontological and material. The gaps are physical too: the heat of data centres and their thirst for water, latency in the cables, unindexed nodes. The call invites speculations, practical interventions and inferences that fill the gaps and expand the diversity of possible communications and communities that can inhabit dark forests, including those built on, against and beneath the infrastructures underlying them, and welcomes work on the (dis-)continuous histories of technological exploration of computational infrastructures over the last 30 years or longer, and on how current artistic, theoretical and technical explorations repeat or break from them. WHO: PhD candidates and early-career researchers, with submissions welcome from researchers inside and outside the academy, including artists, designers and curators. PARTICIPANT EXPECTATIONS: participants write a paper and present it at the workshop, and on the basis of that peer review shorten the research into a newspaper-length article for distribution at the transmediale festival. The workshop is led by scholars from DARC at Aarhus University. DEADLINE: 28 August 2026, 23:59 CEST, via the application link on the call page. Queries to Pablo Velasco, pvelasco[at]cc.au.dk.

Waag Futurelab invites artists, theatre makers, choreographers, dancers, game designers and other creative practitioners to engage directly with seven experimental generative AI Enablers being co-created with technologists and dance, theatre and gaming professionals. The call is an invitation into the development process: selected artists get access to the technologies, datasets, interfaces and assumptions that shape these systems while they are still being built. Rather than testing whether the systems work, artists are asked to interrogate why they work the way they do, who they are designed for, what forms of creativity they enable or constrain, and what assumptions about culture, intelligence, authorship, labour, bodies, audiences and society are embedded in them. Waag is looking for individuals and collectives willing to move beyond adoption into investigation, and welcomes proposals that are speculative, critical, poetic, provocative, humorous, performative, constructive or disruptive, including work that challenges, misuses, reimagines, hacks, subverts or plays with the tools, exposes hidden biases, questions environmental costs, or imagines alternative technological futures. ELIGIBILITY: artists, designers, creative technologists, theatre makers, dancers, choreographers and game designers, as individuals or collectives; applicants must hold a European VAT number.
